title: Transfer of module flattening through a closed immersion
statement: Let $T,V,X$ be schemes, let $p:V\to T$ be locally of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation], and let $j:X\hookrightarrow V$ be a closed immersion over $T$ [def-weil-closed-immersion]. Put $\mathcal F=j_*\mathcal O_X$, with $\mathcal F(H)=\Gamma(j^{-1}H,\mathcal O_X)$ for opens $H\subseteq V$. Let $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_T$ be a finite-type quasi-coherent ideal [pqf-def-coherent], and let $b:T^b=\operatorname{Bl}_{\mathcal I}(T)\to T$ be its blowup [def-nagata-global-blowup]. Put $V_b=V\times_T T^b$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. Let $X^b\subseteq X\times_T T^b$ be the scheme strict transform, using the complement of $V(\mathcal I)$ [def-nagata-strict-transform], and let $j^b:X^b\hookrightarrow V_b$ be the induced closed immersion. Let $\mathcal F^b$ be the module strict transform of $\mathcal F$ [def-trf-module-strict-transform]. There is a canonical isomorphism $\mathcal F^b\cong(j^b)_*\mathcal O_{X^b}$ of $\mathcal O_{V_b}$-modules compatible with their quotient maps from $\mathcal O_{V_b}$. If $\mathcal F^b$ is flat over $T^b$ [def-pc-scheme-module-flat-over] and of finite presentation as an $\mathcal O_{V_b}$-module [def-weil-pbc-module-finite-type-presentation], then $X^b\to T^b$ is flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] and locally of finite presentation. In this case the kernel of $\mathcal O_{V_b}\twoheadrightarrow(j^b)_*\mathcal O_{X^b}$ is locally generated by finitely many sections.

proof.text: Write $P=X\times_TT^b$, let $h:P\to V_b$ be the base change of $j$, and let $k:X^b\hookrightarrow P$ be the strict-transform inclusion, so $j^b=hk$. The affine description of a closed immersion makes $j$ affine, and affine permanence makes $h$ affine. Apply affine strict-transform pushforward to $j$ and $\mathcal O_X$. The structure-sheaf clause of the strict-transform kernel lemma identifies $(\mathcal O_X)^b=k_*\mathcal O_{X^b}$. Composing gives $\mathcal F^b\simeq h_*k_*\mathcal O_{X^b}=(j^b)_*\mathcal O_{X^b}$. These statements apply to the given finite-type centre, without any flatness assumption on $p$ or $j$.

source.place: Tags 080D (1)-(2), definition-strict-transform, and 080G, lemma-strict-transform-affine; flat.tex 081R, final paragraph.

proof.text: For quotient compatibility, affine base change applied to $j$ identifies $p_V^*j_*\mathcal O_X$ with $h_*\mathcal O_P$ as $\mathcal O_{V_b}$-algebras, where $p_V:V_b\to V$. Its unit map is therefore $\mathcal O_{V_b}\to h_*\mathcal O_P$. By the module strict-transform definition the submodule to divide out consists exactly of sections vanishing off the inverse image of the centre. On any open $H\subseteq V_b$ a section of $h_*\mathcal O_P$ vanishes there precisely when the same section on $h^{-1}H$ vanishes off that inverse image. By the structure-sheaf kernel lemma this is $h_*\ker(\mathcal O_P\to k_*\mathcal O_{X^b})$. Apply affine pushforward of quasi-coherent quotients to $h$ and this kernel: it supplies the unique quotient isomorphism carrying the defining projection to $h_*(\mathcal O_P\to k_*\mathcal O_{X^b})$. Thus choose the comparison in Step 1 to be this isomorphism. Both maps from $\mathcal O_{V_b}$ send a local section to its restriction on $X^b$, so the required square commutes. Uniqueness follows from the surjectivity of the defining quotient projection.

source.place: Tags 080D and 080G; coherent.tex Tag 02KG, lemma-affine-base-change. The quotient universal property makes the compatibility explicit.

proof.text: Assume now the two hypotheses on $\mathcal F^b$. For $x\in X^b$ put $v=j^b(x)$ and let $t\in T^b$ be its image. Because a closed immersion is a homeomorphism onto its image, the intersections $H\cap X^b$, for open neighbourhoods $H$ of $v$, are cofinal among neighbourhoods of $x$. Taking the direct limits in the stated formula for pushforward sections gives $((j^b)_*\mathcal O_{X^b})_v=\mathcal O_{X^b,x}$, with the same $\mathcal O_{T^b,t}$-action. Step 1 and the stalk formulation of flatness over the base make this stalk flat over $\mathcal O_{T^b,t}$. This is exactly flatness of $X^b\to T^b$ at $x$; it holds for every $x$.

source.place: Tag 081R, lemma-flat-after-blowing-up, final implication; expanded using the definitions of flatness.

proof.text: Let $\mathcal J=\ker(\mathcal O_{V_b}\twoheadrightarrow(j^b)_*\mathcal O_{X^b})$. Step 1 transfers finite presentation of $\mathcal F^b$ to the target. Apply the finite-kernel lemma with $r=1$ to obtain that $\mathcal J$ is of finite type, which is the last assertion. The strict-transform kernel lemma makes $\mathcal F^b$ quasi-coherent, hence its isomorphic target is quasi-coherent. The kernel theorem then makes $\mathcal J$ quasi-coherent. Consequently on every affine open $H=\operatorname{Spec}B$ of $V_b$, the ideal $J=\mathcal J(H)$ is finitely generated, by the affine finite-type criterion. The closed-immersion affine description gives $(j^b)^{-1}H=\operatorname{Spec}(B/J)$.

To exhibit suitable ambient affine charts, choose an affine $\operatorname{Spec}A\subseteq T$, an affine $\operatorname{Spec}C\subseteq p^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$, and an affine $\operatorname{Spec}R\subseteq b^{-1}(\operatorname{Spec}A)$. These choices cover $V_b$ by the opens $H=\operatorname{Spec}C\times_{\operatorname{Spec}A}\operatorname{Spec}R=\operatorname{Spec}(C\otimes_AR)$. Since $p$ is locally of finite presentation, the affine-open criterion says that $C$ is finitely presented over $A$. The base-change theorem for finitely presented algebras therefore makes $B=C\otimes_AR$ finitely presented over $R$. No noetherian hypothesis is used.

source.place: Tags 01TQ, lemma-locally-finite-presentation-characterize, and 01TS, lemma-base-change-finite-presentation, via affine tensor products.

proof.text: On a chart of Step 5 write $B=R[z_1,\ldots,z_n]/(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$, and choose generators $g_1,\ldots,g_s$ of $J$ from Step 4. Lift each $g_i$ to a polynomial $\widetilde g_i$. The map from the polynomial ring to $B/J$ is surjective and its kernel is $(f_1,\ldots,f_m,\widetilde g_1,\ldots,\widetilde g_s)$: if a polynomial maps into $J$, express its image as $\sum b_i g_i$, lift the $b_i$, and subtract that sum to land in $(f_1,\ldots,f_m)$. Thus $B/J$ is finitely presented over $R$. These affine opens cover $X^b$, and the definition of local finite presentation proves $X^b\to T^b$ locally of finite presentation.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q67-fb3ad6326 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the whole item. The statement is unchanged and matches the Stacks 081R closed-immersion subargument; the item correctly writes T^b where Stacks slips and says S. I read 080D/080G (with its proof), 01BP, 01PB, 01IC, 02KG, 01TQ and 05G5 at their places, and all tags check out. Step 1: j is affine, so h is affine by permanence; 080G applied to j and O_X plus the structure-sheaf clause of the sheaf-kernel lemma give F^b ≅ h_*k_*O = (j^b)_*O. Step 2 writes out the 080G proof: affine base change (2) as an algebra isomorphism, the sectionwise identity for pushing forward supported sections (elementary; lem-trf-supported-sections-pushforward also states it), then the unique θ from the affine quasi-coherent quotient lemma. This gives compatibility with the maps from O_{V_b}, and it makes Step 1's composite redundant, which is harmless. Step 3 gets stalk flatness through the closed-immersion stalk and is correctly marked elementary. Step 4 applies 01BP with r=1 to the surjection O_{V_b}→(j^b)_*O, gets J quasi-coherent from the kernel lemma, finitely generated J(H) from the affine criterion, and identifies the closed-immersion ideal with J(H). Steps 5 and 6: the affine charts cover V_b, B=C⊗_A R is f.p. over R by 01TQ and base change, and B/J=R[z]/(f,g~) is f.p., which gives lfp of X^b. The small cases I tested: I=O, I=0, X empty, X=V, and A=k[t] with X=V(t) where the strict transform is empty. No duplicate turned up in the DAG search. I accept the five tool_uses as generic tools; one of them is a Mathlib leaf. No new nodes, no SGA citations, no changes made.
